 Advertisement ‘Almost our Super Bowl’: Baltimore County sees steady early voting turnout on day one
 Advertisement Updated: 7:35 PM EDT Oct 22, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Kate Amara Reporter ‘Almost our Super Bowl’: Baltimore County sees steady early voting turnout on day one
 Updated: 7:35 PM EDT Oct 22, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Kate Amara Reporter OWINGS MILLS, Md. — Maryland's early voting period for the midterm elections began Thursday, with voters turning out at polling locations across Baltimore County to cast their ballots.
 At the Baltimore County Elections headquarters, the early voting center saw a steady stream of voters throughout the afternoon, while the Honeygo Run Community Center in Perry Hall experienced busier periods in the morning and around lunchtime. 
 Advertisement | COMMITMENT 2026: Gubernatorial election guide | Ballot questions 
 "I voted. Just finished voting," said Cindy McNelly, a Baltimore County voter. "This was, to me, a very streamlined process. Very simple."
 Ruie Lavoie, Baltimore County elections administrator, described the significance of the first day of early voting. 
 "Day one of early voting is like almost our Super Bowl. It's kind of like the playoffs," Lavoie said. 
 The Honeygo Run Community Center was lined with political signs along the main road, parking lot, and grassy areas as voters made their way inside to cast their ballots. 
 Lavoie noted that the process was running smoothly at the county's busiest locations.
 "Things are going very well. Honeygo and Randallstown seem to be the busiest, but the voter flow is moving well, and things are good," Lavoie said. 
 Marylanders can vote early at any early voting center in their county from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily through next Thursday. Other options include voting by mail or heading to the polls on Election Day, Tuesday, Nov. 3. 
 "I do a mail-in ballot, but also want to make sure I hand-delivered it. I didn't want to put it in the dropbox," McClain-Boykin said. 
 Completed ballots can be returned through the post office, official drop boxes, local election offices, any early voting center, or any precinct on Election Day, thanks to recent legal changes.
 According to unofficial numbers, at 4:30 p.m., about 63,000 people had cast a ballot during the first day of early voting.
